title: Why exactly-once is difficult
description: Understand why true exactly-once delivery is impossible in distributed systems and how to achieve exactly-once semantics through idempotency.

data.text: True exactly-once delivery—where a message is delivered exactly one time, never more, never less—is impossible in distributed systems due to the two generals problem and network uncertainty. What we call "exactly-once" is actually at-least-once delivery with idempotent processing.
The impossibility stems from the uncertainty of distributed communication.

items: Network failures—messages can be lost in transit
Uncertain delivery—sender can't know if message arrived before crash
Timeout ambiguity—did the message arrive or not?
Receiver crashes—message received but not processed
Duplicate acknowledgments—ack lost, sender retries

data.title: Two Generals Problem
data.text: In distributed systems, it's impossible to guarantee agreement over an unreliable channel. This fundamental result proves exactly-once delivery is impossible.
Consider what can go wrong in a simple producer-consumer interaction.

items: Message sent, network fails before receipt—at-most-once (loss)
Message received, ack lost, sender retries—at-least-once (duplicate)
Message received, consumer crashes before processing—at-least-once (retry)
Ack received, consumer crashes before persisting—at-least-once (replay)
Message duplicated in queue—at-least-once (duplicate)

data.text: Since we can't prevent duplicates, we make them harmless through idempotency.

items: Assign unique IDs to all messages
Track sent messages to detect duplicates
Use idempotent writes to the message system
Implement transactional outbox pattern
Deduplicate using message IDs
Use conditional database operations
Design idempotent business logic
Track processed message IDs in a deduplication table

data.title: Key Insight
data.text: Exactly-once semantics require end-to-end idempotency. The messaging system can't do it alone—both producer and consumer must participate.
Many systems advertise exactly-once, but they're implementing it through specific patterns.

items: Kafka: Idempotent producers + transactional offsets + consumer idempotency
AWS SQS: Visibility timeout + deduplication ID
Google Pub/Sub: Exactly-once delivery with deduplication
Azure Service Bus: Duplicate detection
All of these: At-least-once + deduplication, not true exactly-once

items.title: Deduplication Table
items.description: Store processed message IDs. Check before processing. Simple but requires additional storage and cleanup.

items.title: Idempotent Operations
items.description: Make operations safe to repeat. Use conditional updates, unique constraints, or naturally idempotent operations.

items.title: Transactional Outbox
items.description: Write to database and message queue atomically. Guarantees message is only sent once per transaction.

items.title: Stateful Streaming
items.description: Track processing state in the stream system (e.g., Kafka transactions). Requires stream processor support.

items: Exactly-once semantics add complexity and overhead
Requires coordination across multiple components
May impact performance due to deduplication checks
Not always necessary—evaluate if you really need it
Often simpler to use at-least-once with idempotency
